name: Executive order of January 20, 1857 establishing the Muckleshoot reservation
promises: After a later meeting at Fox Island between Governor Stevens and principal men of the Nisqually, Stevens recommended a new reservation on Muckleshoot Prairie, and the President approved it on January 20, 1857; the Commission found the reservation was not established as a result of the Point Elliott or Medicine Creek treaties (ICC Docket 98, finding 8).
The reservation was given metes and bounds by executive order of April 9, 1874; it then held 3,532.72 acres (ICC Docket 98, finding 8).

breaches.what: The Muckleshoot Indian Tribe says the Indians at the 1856 Fox Island meeting understood that a wedge of land beginning at the junction of the White and Green Rivers would be part of the reservation, but the documents behind the January 20, 1857 order refer only to Muckleshoot Prairie.
breaches.quote: the documents that led to the Executive Order of January 20, 1857, only refer to the Muckleshoot Prairie

compensation: In Docket 98 the Indian Claims Commission held the Muckleshoot entitled to compensation for their ancestors' aboriginal land taken as of March 8, 1859, when the Point Elliott treaty took effect, and in 1958 found it worth $86,377.00. The offsets were compromised at $6,000.00 and a final judgment of $80,377.00 was entered on October 18, 1963. That claim was for land outside the reservation.
today: The Tribe says the reservation was enlarged by the 1874 order, allotted in 1904 to 16 families leaving no land in tribal hands, and that it has been reacquiring land within the reservation since, to nearly 4,000 acres by 2020.

nationVoice.summary: The Tribe says the 1857 order covered only Muckleshoot Prairie and a military station, leaving out land the Indians at Fox Island understood was included, and that 1904 allotment left no land in tribal hands until its own reacquisition.

Audit 2026-11-08: first promise and plain.promised corrected: finding 8 says the reservation came from the Fox Island meeting with the Nisqually and was NOT established under the Point Elliott or Medicine Creek treaty, so "for Indians under the Medicine Creek treaty" was not supported by the cited finding. Judgment figure added: $86,377.00 value less $6,000.00 compromised offsets, final judgment $80,377.00 (same-day opinion and findings, ids 867 and 853; attorney fee findings, id 1528, repeat $80,377.00). Tribe quote checked exact.

plain.promised: In 1857, after a council at Fox Island, the President set aside a reservation on Muckleshoot Prairie.
plain.happened: The Muckleshoot Tribe says the order left out land between the White and Green Rivers that its ancestors understood was included. No court or government finding was located.
plain.today: The reservation was enlarged in 1874, then allotted in 1904; the Tribe has been buying back land, to nearly 4,000 acres by 2020.
